title: Timebound ephemeral admin provisioning and audited privilege escrow
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create a timebound, auditable workflow for granting emergency elevated privileges without creating long-lived admin accounts. This ticket implements a Privilege Escrow Service (PES) that issues ephemeral credentials tied to SSO assertions and RBAC-v2 entitlements, logs a high-fidelity audit trail, and enforces multi-party approval and automatic revocation. The goal is to reduce blast radius from ad-hoc break-glass actions while preserving rapid incident response for oncall and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: PES issues ephemeral admin tokens capped by scope and TTL (max 4 hours) and tokens are bound to a single SSO session ID
All issuance and use events are recorded in the audit pipeline with user, approvers, reason, TTL, requested scope, IP, and session metadata
Two-step approval required by default for production-scoped elevation; emergency single-approver flow allowed under oncall+manager override but flagged for retrospective review
Tokens automatically revoked on TTL expiry, logout, or manual revocation; revocations emit audit events and invalidate active sessions within 30s
Integration tests validate RBAC v2 policy enforcement when ephemeral creds are used and fall back to least-privilege paths if denied
design_notes: Use RBAC-v2 roles and entitlements as source-of-truth for scope calculation. PES maps requested scopes to existing role IDs instead of creating transient roles.
Bind tokens to SAML assertion IDs and OAuth session IDs. Store only fingerprints in PES to avoid sensitive persistence.
Support two issuance modes: 'Canary' (audited, requires approver) and 'Immediate' (single approver for SRE oncall). Both flows create a post-event ticket for retrospective audit.
Audit log format follows common schema used by observability team: timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, approver_ids, scope_ids, ttl_seconds, reason, ip, session_fingerprint, request_id
Avoid storing raw tokens or private keys in DB; use short-lived keyed HSM envelopes and one-way indexes for lookup
implementation_plan: Schema: Add PES_issuance_events table with indexed fields for session_fingerprint and request_id
API: POST /internal/pes/issue with SSO assertion, requested_scope, reason, approver_ids(optional) -> returns ephemeral credential and audit request_id
Approval Service: Small approval microservice that can call Slack approval workflow and persist approver attestations
Authn/Authz: Modify auth middleware to accept PES tokens and validate TTL + scope against RBAC-v2 policy engine
Audit pipeline: Emit CES-compatible events to kafka topic audit.events.pes and wire into log retention (90d) and cold storage (7y for enterprise customers)
Rotation: Create cron job to scan for leaked/stale sessions and force revoke older-than-policy thresholds
Infra: HSM/KMS integration for token signing and one-time decryption, use KMS key alias 'pes/signing/2026'
rollout_plan: Alpha: Internal SRE and Platform team only (feature flag pes.alpha=true) - 1 week
Beta: Invite-only trial with security champions and two pilot customers - 3 weeks
GA: Default enabled for orgs with RBAC-v2 and SSO; configurable TTL and approval policies via Console policies page
Backout: feature flag rollback, revoke all active PES tokens, and switch clients to fallback managed-admin path
test_plan: Unit tests: PES API validation, TTL handling, database index behavior
Integration tests: Issue -> Approve -> Use token against protected endpoints, verify audit events produced
Chaos: Simulate PES DB failover and ensure fallback denies issuance and records incident
Pen test: Run targeted privilege escalation attempt and confirm token binding prevents reuse
E2E: Oncall runbook drills to exercise issuance, revocation, and retrospective audits
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: pes.tokens_issued_total (label: scope, approver_mode) -> alert on spike > 5x baseline
Metric: pes.revocations_total -> alert if manual revocations > threshold in 1h
Log: Audit event success/failure => routed to security SIEM; create SIEM rule to flag single-approver production scopes
Datadog dashboard: PES issuance latency, approval latency, active_tokens_count
Pager: SOC oncall paged for suspected token leakage (>=3 tokens from same IP not tied to SSO session)
docs_and_training: Confluence runbook: 'Privilege Escrow Service - issuance and post-incident review' (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/PES+Runbook)
Playbook: Oncall steps for emergency elevation, sample justification text to include in request
Training: 30-minute security workshop for SRE and support on new flows
Console docs: UI controls for configuring approval policy and TTL with screenshots
